precepts.text: Fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth. Frolic produces an image of comfort that is false: the athlete making millions running up and down the court thinks he has made it, but the real soul knows he is still a slave. Kaepernick caught the fever and stood up, and they made an example of him; his teammates know he was right and pretend to be fine. That pretence is fear. We cannot drown out the squeaking of our wretched condition with frolic, drugs, alcohol, or music, dancing slaves made to look whole while the spirit rots.
precepts.point: The squeaky wheel gets the oil. We will complain, judge, bring out the records, and beg the Lord until he kills our enemies and sets us up, like the widow before the unjust judge. Our enemies want us silent, locked away with our mouths zipped, calling us troublemakers; yes, we are causing trouble, because you are not supposed to be over us. Nehemiah 2:10 shows they grieve when a man comes to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.

note.label: The Image of Dysfunction or the Image of God Which One Are You?

precepts.why:
“For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth.” Succours means comforts. Fear is a betraying comfort.

We are encouraged to be sports figures, entertainers and dancers, to frolic: to play, jump and move about in a happy, lively, carefree way, and never think about anything serious, because then we become a danger. Frolic produces an image of comfort that is false. The athlete makes millions running up and down the court and thinks he has made it, but the real soul of him knows he is still a slave. Keeping us in the silly mode makes us consumers, not people who run our own banks and medical centers.

Kaepernick caught the fever. He looked at what was happening to his people while he was up there throwing the ball, got serious and stood up, and you saw how they dealt with him. His teammates know he did the right thing, but they have to pretend they are all right. That pretending is the fear: they stay in that mess and never stand up to be men, lying to themselves that they are comfortable being clowns.

So the watchmen of Isaiah 62 cannot hold their peace. We cannot drown out the horrible squeaking of our wretched condition, the psychological traumas we live through, with frolic, drugs, alcohol or music. We cannot be dancing slaves made to look whole while inside there is a spiritual rot we can no longer afford. We must stand up and be real men and women, keep not silence, and give the Lord no rest.

precepts.text: So then whosoever there fell down was straitway kept shut up in a prison without iron bars. Now this is about ancient Egypt, but watch what it says about the Egyptians, and how it relates to us. Just like the ancient Egyptians were in that sea of darkness, it says they were shut up in a prison without iron bars. That is what we are in today. There are no iron bars, and people say, I am free, there are no shackles on me. It is the same thing.
precepts.point: By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison. We are the spirits in prison that he preached to. You have Christians talking about, did he go under the ground? No. We are in a prison house. Being dominated by another race is a prison. Christ came to us while Rome dominated us and he preached to us.
precepts.why:
Christ “went and preached unto the spirits in prison”. We are the spirits in prison that he preached to. Christians ask, did he go under the ground? No. Being dominated by another race is a prison, and Christ came to us while Rome dominated us and preached to us.

Wisdom shows what kind of prison it is. This is about ancient Egypt, but watch what it says about the Egyptians and how it relates to us: “So then whosoever there fell down was straitly kept, shut up in a prison without iron bars”. Just like the ancient Egyptians in that sea of darkness were shut up in a prison without iron bars, that is what we are in today. There are no iron bars, so people say, I'm free, there are no shackles on me. It is the same thing.

Isaiah said we are “hid in prison houses”, and those prison houses are democracy, Republicans, socialism, liberals, Baptists, Episcopal. So the message for our people is Isaiah 49:9: “That thou mayest say to the prisoners, Go forth; to them that are in darkness, Shew yourselves.” Come out of that cage.

And Zechariah shows the way out: “by the blood of thy covenant I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water.” The blood of the covenant is Christ dying on the cross. The prisoners are you and me; the pit is Babylon, where there is no water, no truth being taught besides what we are teaching. “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”: the stronghold is the commandments in the name of Christ. The Christ who preached to the spirits in prison is the one who brings us out of this prison without bars.

precepts.text: For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth. A soldier broke it down: you trick yourself into being scared because you make up things in your mind which are not really there. And you also have a lack of faith: your faith is supposed to be in the Lord, but a lot of the time your faith is only in what you can see with your eyes.
precepts.point: This is the king. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him? If the officer is fearful, it spreads to the soldiers under him.
precepts.why:
Saul saw the host of the Philistines and “was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.” What is fear? “For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth.”

A soldier broke it down: the succours go into comfort, and fear betrays that comfort. What reason offers is the lies you make up in your head. You trick yourself into being scared, because you make up things in your mind which ain’t really there.

And on top of that, fear is a lack of faith. Your faith is supposed to be in the Lord, but a lot of the time your faith is basically what you can see with your eyes. Saul looked at the host of the Philistines with his eyes and his heart trembled, instead of trusting the Lord who had made him king.
